title: Persistent and Ephemeral Volumes

header.html: Kubernetes v1.37.0 (3-node test cluster, containerd 2.3.4, local-path default StorageClass)

toc.title: hostPath (and why it is rarely right)

html:
1Two kinds of volume

A container's own file system is thrown away when the container restarts. A volume is a directory that is mounted into one or more containers of a Pod, in two steps: the Pod lists it under spec.volumes, and each container that wants it lists it under volumeMounts with a mountPath.

Kind Examples Lifetime
Ephemeral emptyDir, configMap, secret, projected, downwardAPI the Pod's life: gone when the Pod is deleted
Persistent persistentVolumeClaim (PV/PVC), hostPath for a single node beyond the Pod: the data stays 
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    volumeMounts:
    - name: cache            # must match a volume name
      mountPath: /cache
      # readOnly: true     # optional; subPath: sub-dir  mounts one folder of the volume
  volumes:
  - name: cache
    emptyDir: {}

2Ephemeral volumes

Volume Use
emptyDir scratch space created empty when the Pod starts, shared by its containers; survives a container restart but not the Pod's deletion
emptyDir with medium: Memory a RAM-backed tmpfs; counts against the container's memory; fast
emptyDir with sizeLimit the Pod is evicted if it uses more
configMap, secret configuration files and credentials as files (Module 9)
downwardAPI the Pod's own name, labels, limits as files
projected several sources (ConfigMap, Secret, token, downward API) in one directory 
volumes:
- name: cache
  emptyDir:
    medium: Memory
    sizeLimit: 64Mi

3hostPath (and why it is rarely right)

A hostPath volume mounts a directory of the node:

volumes:
- name: node-data
  hostPath:
    path: /opt/ckad-data
    type: DirectoryOrCreate      # Directory, File, FileOrCreate, Socket ...

The data stays on that node only. If the Pod moves to another node, it sees a different directory. It also exposes the node's file system, so security rules often forbid it. Use it for node-level agents and for exam tasks that ask for it; use a PersistentVolumeClaim for application data.

4Persistent volumes, claims and StorageClasses

Object Who creates it What it is
PersistentVolume (PV) an administrator, or a provisioner a piece of storage; cluster-wide (no namespace)
PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) the developer a request for storage of a size and access mode; namespaced
StorageClass an administrator a recipe for creating PVs on demand ("dynamic provisioning")

Binding. A claim binds to a PV that has enough capacity, a compatible access mode and the same storageClassName. Once bound, they belong to each other (the PV shows Bound and a claimRef). A Pod then mounts the claim, not the volume.

Access mode Short Meaning
ReadWriteOnce RWO read-write by one node
ReadOnlyMany ROX read-only by many nodes
ReadWriteMany RWX read-write by many nodes
ReadWriteOncePod RWOP read-write by one Pod
Reclaim policy (on the PV) When the claim is deleted
Retain the PV and its data are kept; it is Released and must be cleaned by hand
Delete the PV and the storage are deleted (the default for dynamic volumes)

Static provisioning (an administrator creates the PV):

apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata: {name: pv-reports}
spec:
  capacity: {storage: 2Gi}
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: manual
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  hostPath: {path: /mnt/reports}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: pvc-reports, namespace: vol}
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: manual
  resources: {requests: {storage: 1Gi}}

Dynamic provisioning (no PV is written by hand): omit storageClassName to get the cluster's default StorageClass (marked (default) in k get sc), or name a class. The provisioner creates the PV when the claim is used. On this test cluster the class standard (local-path) uses WaitForFirstConsumer: the claim stays Pending until a Pod uses it, and that is normal, not an error.

Using the claim in a Pod:

volumes:
- name: store
  persistentVolumeClaim:
    claimName: data

Common failures

Symptom Cause Fix
PVC Pending, event says storage class not found storageClassName names a class that does not exist recreate the PVC with a real class or none (storageClassName cannot be edited)
PVC Pending, no PV matches size, access mode or class mismatch with every PV fix the claim or the PV
PVC Pending with WaitForFirstConsumer no Pod uses it yet create the Pod
Pod Pending, "unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims" the claim is not bound fix the claim first
Data gone after deleting the Pod the data was on an emptyDir use a PVC

You can add a PVC to a Deployment the same way, but a ReadWriteOnce volume can be mounted from one node at a time: several replicas on different nodes will not all start. A StatefulSet gives each replica its own claim with volumeClaimTemplates.

Exam tip

. To make a claim bind to a specific PV in a task, give both the same storageClassName and a compatible size and mode. A claim without a class gets the default class and will not bind to a PV whose class is manual.

Exam tip

. kubectl get pv,pvc -A shows the whole picture; kubectl describe pvc <name> has the reason in its events.

5Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m04 -->

Lab 4.1: emptydir memory

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m04-01-emptydir-memory)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace vol, create a Pod named scratch with one container (image busybox:1.36, command sleep 3600) that has an ephemeral volume named cache mounted at /cache. The volume must live in memory (medium: Memory) and be limited to 64Mi. Wait until the Pod is Running.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n vol apply -f - <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: scratch
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: cache, mountPath: /cache}
  volumes:
  - name: cache
    emptyDir:
      medium: Memory
      sizeLimit: 64Mi
Y
kubectl -n vol wait --for=condition=Ready pod/scratch --timeout=120s
kubectl -n vol exec scratch -- df /cache

Lab 4.2: hostpath

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 5 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m04-02-hostpath)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace vol, create a Pod named hp (image busybox:1.36) whose container runs sh -c "echo hello from pod > /host-data/hello.txt; sleep 3600". Mount the node directory /opt/ckad-data (create it if it does not exist, type: DirectoryOrCreate) with a hostPath volume at /host-data in the container. The file must appear in /opt/ckad-data on the node that runs the Pod.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n vol apply -f - <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: hp
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh", "-c", "echo hello from pod > /host-data/hello.txt; sleep 3600"]
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: node-data, mountPath: /host-data}
  volumes:
  - name: node-data
    hostPath:
      path: /opt/ckad-data
      type: DirectoryOrCreate
Y
kubectl -n vol wait --for=condition=Ready pod/hp --timeout=120s
sleep 3
node=$(kubectl -n vol get pod hp -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}')
docker exec $node cat /opt/ckad-data/hello.txt

Lab 4.3: pv pvc static

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 8 | Time: about 9 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m04-03-pv-pvc-static)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

Create a PersistentVolume named pv-reports (capacity 2Gi, access mode ReadWriteOnce, storageClassName: manual, reclaim policy Retain, hostPath /mnt/reports). In the namespace vol, create a PersistentVolumeClaim named pvc-reports that requests 1Gi with ReadWriteOnce and storageClassName: manual, and a Pod named reporter (image busybox:1.36, command sleep 3600) that mounts the claim at /reports. The claim must be bound to pv-reports and the Pod Running.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl apply -f - <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: pv-reports
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 2Gi
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: manual
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  hostPath:
    path: /mnt/reports
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: pvc-reports
  namespace: vol
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: manual
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: reporter
  namespace: vol
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: reports, mountPath: /reports}
  volumes:
  - name: reports
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: pvc-reports
Y
kubectl -n vol wait --for=condition=Ready pod/reporter --timeout=120s
kubectl -n vol get pvc

Lab 4.4: dynamic pvc persists

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 7 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m04-04-dynamic-pvc-persists)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace vol, create a PersistentVolumeClaim named data that requests 1Gi with ReadWriteOnce from the cluster's default StorageClass (do not name a class). Create a Pod writer (image busybox:1.36) that mounts it at /data and runs sh -c "echo kept-after-delete > /data/note.txt; sleep 3600". When the file exists, delete the Pod writer and create a Pod reader (image busybox:1.36, command sleep 3600) that mounts the same claim at /data. The file must still be there.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n vol apply -f - <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: data
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: writer
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh", "-c", "echo kept-after-delete > /data/note.txt; sleep 3600"]
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: store, mountPath: /data}
  volumes:
  - name: store
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: data
Y
kubectl -n vol wait --for=condition=Ready pod/writer --timeout=180s
sleep 3
kubectl -n vol delete pod writer --wait=true
kubectl -n vol apply -f - <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: reader
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: store, mountPath: /data}
  volumes:
  - name: store
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: data
Y
kubectl -n vol wait --for=condition=Ready pod/reader --timeout=180s
kubectl -n vol exec reader -- cat /data/note.txt

Lab 4.5: fix pending pvc

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 6 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m04-05-fix-pending-pvc)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace vol, the Pod db is Pending because its PersistentVolumeClaim db-data cannot be bound (the manifest is ~/work/db.yaml). Fix the problem so that the claim is bound by the cluster's default StorageClass and the Pod is Running. Keep the names, the size (1Gi) and the access mode (ReadWriteOnce).

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n vol describe pvc db-data | tail -5
kubectl get storageclass
kubectl delete -f ~/work/db.yaml --wait=true
sed -i '/storageClassName: fast/d' ~/work/db.yaml
kubectl apply -f ~/work/db.yaml
kubectl -n vol wait --for=condition=Ready pod/db --timeout=180s

<!-- /LABS -->

6Recall questions

R1What is the difference between emptyDir and a PersistentVolumeClaim?

Show the answer

An emptyDir lives and dies with the Pod; a claim's data outlives the Pod.

R2What does medium: Memory do on an emptyDir?

Show the answer

It makes the volume a RAM-backed tmpfs.

R3When does a PVC bind to a PV?

Show the answer

When the PV has enough capacity, a compatible access mode and the same storageClassName.

R4What does the Retain reclaim policy do?

Show the answer

It keeps the PV and its data after the claim is deleted.

R5What happens if a PVC omits storageClassName?

Show the answer

It uses the cluster's default StorageClass.

R6Why is a claim Pending with the WaitForFirstConsumer binding mode?

Show the answer

It waits until a Pod uses it; that is normal.

R7Which access mode allows read-write from one node only?

Show the answer

ReadWriteOnce.

R8Can you change storageClassName on an existing PVC?

Show the answer

No; delete the claim and create it again.

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Mount volumes in the Pod, volumeMounts + mountPath in the container
Ephemeral emptyDir (medium: Memory, sizeLimit), configMap, secret, projected
hostPath node directory; type: DirectoryOrCreate; data stays on that node
PV / PVC / class PV cluster-wide, PVC namespaced, StorageClass makes PVs on demand
Bind rule capacity, access mode and storageClassName must fit
Access modes RWO, ROX, RWX, RWOP
Reclaim Retain keeps data; Delete removes the volume
Pending PVC describe pvc events; wrong class; no consumer yet
